ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows a pyramid made of cubes. On the left is a 3D view with a red path drawn over the cube surfaces. On the right is the top view, labeled “Ansicht von oben,” where the red line goes straight across the pyramid through five cube-width positions: an outer/base position, a middle-level position, the central/top-cube position, another middle-level position, and another outer/base position. Reasoning: Treat the diagram as a vertical cross-section along the red line. Along this cross-section, the ant travels over 5 horizontal cube-side lengths across top faces. At each change of height between levels, it also travels up or down one vertical cube-side length. There are 4 such height changes: up from base to middle, up from middle to top, down from top to middle, and down from middle to base. So the path contains 5 horizontal segments + 4 vertical segments = 9 cube-side segments. Each cube side is 10 cm, so the total distance is 9 × 10 = 90 cm.
